Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. questions.questionText: A sky diver falls vertically from a stationary balloon. She leaves the balloon at time t = 0. At time t = T, she reaches terminal velocity. Beyond the time shown in the graphs, she opens her parachute. Which graph shows the variation with time t of the force F due to air resistance?

options.A: B C D F F F F 0 0 0 0 0 T t 0 T t 0 T t 0 T t

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an arrangement to stop trains that are travelling too fast. speed 50 m s–1 direction maximum speed of travel 10 m s–1 train marker 1 marker 2 Trains coming from the left travel at a speed of 50ms–1. At marker 1, the driver must apply the brakes so that the train decelerates uniformly in order to pass marker 2 at no more than 10ms–1. The train carries a detector that notes the times when the train passes each marker and will apply an emergency brake if the time between passing marker 1 and marker 2 is less than 20s. How far from marker 2 should marker 1 be placed?

options.A: 200m B 400m C 500m D 600m Space for working

questions.questionText: A ball is released from rest above a horizontal surface and bounces several times. The graph shows how, for this ball, a quantity y varies with time. y time What is the quantity y?

A strong wind of speed 33ms–1 blows against a wall. The density of the air is 1.2kgm–3. The wall has an area of 12m2 at right angles to the wind velocity. The air has its speed reduced to zero when it hits the wall. What is the approximate force exerted by the air on the wall?

options.A: 330N B 400N C 480N D 16000N Space for working

questions.questionText: A submarine is in equilibrium in a fully submerged position. sea steel water air What causes the upthrust on the submarine?

options.A: The air in the submarine is less dense than sea water.
options.B: The sea water exerts a greater upward force on the submarine than the weight of the steel.
options.C: The submarine displaces its own volume of sea water.
options.D: There is a difference in water pressure acting on the top and on the bottom of the submarine. Space for working

questions.questionText: A vehicle is at rest on a slope. It is considered to have three forces acting on it to keep it in equilibrium. They are its weight W, a normal reaction force R and a frictional force F. Which triangle of forces is correct?

options.A: B C D F F R R W W W W R R F F

questions.questionText: All external forces on a body cancel out. Which statement must be correct?

options.B: The momentum of the body remains unchanged.
options.C: The speed of the body remains unchanged.
options.D: The total energy (kinetic and potential) of the body remains unchanged. Space for working

questions.questionText: A uniform beam of mass 1.4kg is pivoted at P as shown. The beam has a length of 0.60m and P is 0.20m from one end. Loads of 3.0kg and 6.0kg are suspended 0.35m and 0.15m from the pivot as shown. 0.40 m 0.20 m 0.35 m 0.15 m P 3.0 kg 6.0 kg centre of beam of mass 1.4 kg What torque must be applied to the beam in order to maintain it in equilibrium?
A ball is thrown vertically upwards. Neglecting air resistance, which statement is correct?

options.A: The kinetic energy of the ball is greatest at the greatest height attained.
options.B: By the principle of conservation of energy, the total energy of the ball is constant throughout its motion.
options.C: By the principle of conservation of momentum, the momentum of the ball is constant throughout its motion.
options.D: The potential energy of the ball increases uniformly with time during its ascent.

questions.questionText: A bow of mass 400g shoots an arrow of mass 120g vertically upwards. The potential energy stored in the bow just before release is 80J. The system has an efficiency of 28%. What is the height reached by the arrow when air resistance is neglected?

options.A: 4m B 19m C 187m D 243m Space for working

questions.questionText: A train on a mountain railway is carrying 200 people of average mass 70kg up a slope at an angle of 30° to the horizontal and at a speed of 6.0ms–1. The train itself has a mass of 80000kg. The percentage of the power from the engine which is used to raise the passengers and the train is 40%. What is the power of the engine?

A gas is enclosed inside a cylinder which is fitted with a frictionless piston. V p p heat gas V Initially, the gas has a volume V and is in equilibrium with an external pressure p. The gas is then heated slowly so that it expands, pushing the piston back until the volume of the gas has increased to V . How much work is done by the gas during this expansion?

options.A: p(V – V ) B 1p(V – V ) C p(V + V ) D 1p(V + V )

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an ice cube floating in water. ice Both the ice cube and the water are at 0°C. Which statement correctly compares the molecular properties of the ice and those of the water?

options.A: The mean inter-molecular potential energies are the same for both the ice molecules and the water molecules.
options.B: The mean inter-molecular separations are the same for both the ice and the water.
options.C: The mean kinetic energies are the same for both the ice molecules and the water molecules.
options.D: The mean total energies are the same for both the ice molecules and the water molecules. Space for working

questions.questionText: Two bulbs X and Y containing air at different pressures are connected by a tube P which contains two mercury threads. air pressure air pressure
What is the unit of the Young modulus?

options.A: Nm–1 B Nm C Nm–2 D Nm2 Space for working

questions.questionText: A rubber cord hangs from a rigid support. A weight attached to its lower end is gradually increased from zero, and then gradually reduced to zero. force stretching rubber cord contraction weight extension The force-extension curve for contraction is below the force-extension curve for stretching. What does the shaded area between the curves represent?

options.A: the amount of elastic energy stored in the rubber
options.B: the amount of thermal energy dissipated in the rubber
options.C: the work done on the rubber cord during stretching
options.D: the work done by the rubber cord during contraction Space for working

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a large crane on a construction site lifting a cube-shaped load. cable crane load
The order of magnitude of the frequency of the shortest wavelength of visible light waves can be x expressed as 10 Hz. What is the value of x?

options.A: 12 B 13 C 14 D 15 Space for working

What is correct for all transverse waves?

options.C: They can all travel through a vacuum.
options.D: They all involve the oscillation of atoms. Space for working

questions.questionText: A transmitter of electromagnetic waves is placed 45cm from a reflective surface. reflective surface transmitter 45 cm The emitted waves have a frequency of 1.00GHz. A stationary wave is produced with a node at the transmitter and a node at the surface. How many antinodes are in the space between the transmitter and the surface?

A teacher sets up the apparatus shown to demonstrate a two-slit interference pattern on the screen. double screen single slit slit source q of light p r Which change to the apparatus will increase the fringe spacing?

options.D: decreasing the wavelength of the light Space for working

questions.questionText: Monochromatic light of wavelength 5.30 × 10–7m is incident normally on a diffraction grating. The first order maximum is observed at an angle of 15.4° to the direction of the incident light. What is the angle between the first and second order diffraction maxima?

Two conducting layers of a liquid crystal display of a calculator are 8µm apart. A 1.5V cell is connected across the conducting layers when the calculator is switched on. What is the electric field strength between the layers?
A positively-charged particle is projected into a uniform electric field. Which diagram represents the path of the particle in the electric field?

options.C: D + + electric field in plane of the paper electric field in plane of the paper electric field into paper electric field into paper

questions.questionText: A power cable has length 2000m. The cable is made of twelve parallel strands of copper wire, each with diameter 0.51mm. What is the resistance of the cable? (resistivity of copper = 1.7 × 10–8Ωm)

A low-voltage supply with an e.m.f. of 20V and an internal resistance of 1.5Ω is used to supply power to a heater of resistance 6.5Ω in a fish tank. What is the power supplied to the water in the fish tank?

options.A: 41W B 50W C 53W D 62W Space for working

questions.questionText: A filament lamp has a resistance of 180Ω when the current in it is 500mA. What is the power transformed in the lamp?

Two wires P and Q made of the same material are connected to the same electrical supply. P has twice the length of Q and one-third of the diameter of Q, as shown in the diagram. P d 2l Q 3d l current in P What is the ratio ? current in Q

Five resistors are connected as shown.
